record.paper_title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
record.original_question: How can one give concrete physical interpretations for the infinitely many symmetries and conservation laws that arise in integrable systems, beyond the small subset that already have familiar interpretations such as space-time translation invariance, Galilean or Lorentz invariance, scaling invariance, and the conservation of mass, momentum, and energy?

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 1: Physical explanations of infinitely many symmetries and conservation laws
The elucidation of the physical interpretations of the infinitely many symmetries and conservation laws inherent to integrable systems represents a profound and enduring question at the intersection of physics and mathematics. While it is widely acknowledged that integrable systems are characterized by an infinitely many symmetries and conservation laws, only a select few possess explicit, tangible physical interpretations, such as those related to space-time translational invariance, Galilean or Lorentz invariance, scaling invariance, as well as the conservation of mass, momentum, and energy.

artifact.self_contained_problem: An integrable nonlinear partial differential equation (such as the Korteweg–de Vries, nonlinear Schrödinger, or Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation) typically admits an infinite hierarchy of commuting symmetries and an associated infinite sequence of independent conservation laws. A small number of these symmetries and conserved quantities possess well-known physical interpretations: space–time translation invariance (yielding conservation of momentum and energy), Galilean or Lorentz invariance, scaling invariance, and conservation of mass. However, the overwhelming majority of the higher-order members of these infinite hierarchies have no presently known physical interpretation.\n\nProblem. Provide concrete physical interpretations for the higher (non-classical) members of the infinite hierarchies of symmetries and conservation laws of integrable systems. More precisely, develop a systematic framework that, given an integrable evolution equation and its infinite sequence of commuting flows (symmetries) {K_n}_{n≥1} and conserved densities {ρ_n}_{n≥1}, associates to each K_n and each ρ_n a physically meaningful quantity (for instance, an invariance principle, a measurable observable, or a transformation of physical variables) generalizing the known cases of translations, Galilean/Lorentz boosts, scalings, and conservation of mass, momentum, and energy.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a longstanding open problem in the theory of integrable systems. While partial physical interpretations exist for certain higher symmetries (e.g., in connection with generalized hydrodynamics and quasi-local charges in integrable quantum systems), no general framework giving physical meaning to all members of the infinite symmetry/conservation-law hierarchies is known. The problem remains open.
